Message: SBC GPIO MAPPING
A0..A7 and B0..B7 are logical compatibility channel names inherited from Glasgow.
They are not Raspberry Pi BCM numbers and they are not physical header-pin numbers.
Logical channel                 Purpose
A0..A7                         Pump-power output
B0..B7                         Comparator/status input
SBC.GPIO.<logical channel>     Raspberry Pi BCM GPIO number
EXAMPLE
VacuumPumps.write=A0 and SBC.GPIO.A0=17
-> equipment power output uses BCM GPIO17
-> BCM GPIO17 is physical header pin 11
VacuumPumps.read=B0 and SBC.GPIO.B0=27
-> equipment status input uses BCM GPIO27
-> BCM GPIO27 is physical header pin 13
CHANGING THE EQUIPMENT COUNT
- The equipment list is configuration-driven.
- Configure a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 8 VacuumPumps items.
- Every equipment item requires one unused logical A output and one unused logical B input.
- Add both logical channel names to SBC.GPIO and assign two unused BCM GPIO numbers.
- Equipment names, write channels, read channels, and BCM GPIO assignments must be unique.
- Every configured write/read channel must have a corresponding SBC.GPIO entry.
SELECTING RASPBERRY PI GPIO
Use BCM numbering, not physical header-pin numbering.
Inspect the actual SBC before assigning pins:
pinout
pinctrl get
gpioinfo
Common general-purpose candidates:
BCM       Common alternate use
0, 1      HAT EEPROM identification; avoid
2, 3      I2C SDA/SCL with fixed pull-ups
7-11      SPI
14, 15    Serial UART
18-21     Audio, PWM, or PCM on some configurations
An alternate-function pin may be used as ordinary GPIO only when its interface and device-tree overlay are disabled.
ELECTRICAL SAFETY
- Raspberry Pi GPIO uses 3.3 V logic.
- Raspberry Pi GPIO inputs are not 5 V tolerant.
- Never connect pumps, contactors, solenoids, or relay coils directly to GPIO.
- Use galvanically isolated and appropriately rated input/output interface circuitry.
- Provide hardware-defined safe output states during boot, shutdown, and SBC power loss.
COMMISSIONING WARNING
The committed SBC.GPIO values are initial assignments only.
Verify every BCM-to-physical-pin connection against the final Raspberry Pi model, carrier schematic, relay interface, and wiring drawing before changing Simulate to false.
